papers.title_in_file: Machine Learning Assisted Cognitive Construction of a Shallow Depth Dynamic Ansatz for Noisy Quantum Hardware
papers.what_it_is: Uses a restricted Boltzmann machine plus perturbation-theory filtering to build shallow VQE ansatzes for molecules.

assertions.value: The authors report that the RBM-generated ansatz reaches an energy very close to conventional dUCCSDT while using exceptionally fewer CNOT gates, and even fewer than conventional dUCCSD, on the tested molecules.
quotes: the energy obtained after variationally optimizing RBMdUCCSDTS is very close to that obtained using conventional dUCCSDT
all while using exceptionally fewer CNOT gates (a measure of circuit depth). The former even has fewer CNOT gates than conventional dUCCSD.

assertions.value: The authors report CNOT gate counts of 1912, 1848, 3896, and 19640 in the energy-versus-evaluations comparison for BH, in the order of the methods listed in the caption.
quotes: The corresponding CNOT gate counts are 1912, 1848, 3896, and 19640, respectively.

assertions.value: The authors state that the RBM energy is not below conventional dUCCSDT for any tested system, and that the noisy runs use a VQE in a noisy backend built from a noise model.
quotes: As the energy for RBM-dUCCSDTS is not below the conventional dUCCSDT for any of the tested systems
we implement RBMdUCCSDTS to calculate the ground state energy using VQE in a noisy backend.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section III.B states the noisy setup
assertions.reader_inference: The noise model is imported from a fake (simulated) IBM backend per the section text, so the noisy results are simulated, not real hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Speedups for Bayesian Network Structure Learning
papers.what_it_is: Gives quantum algorithms for exact Bayesian network structure learning with a polynomial speedup, and a SETH lower-bound argument for classical ones.

assertions.value: The paper gives two quantum algorithms for exact BNSL whose running time has a base below the classical base, a polynomial quantum speedup under assumptions on the number of potential parent sets.
quotes: We answer the question in the affirmative by giving two algorithms
This gives a polynomial speedup as long as F grows subexponentially or very moderately exponentially in n.
assertions.certainty_reason: Algorithms with running-time analysis, Sections 3 and 4

assertions.value: The paper proves that one presumably cannot lower the base 2 for any classical algorithm, as that would refute the strong exponential time hypothesis.
quotes: We also prove that one presumably cannot lower the base 2 for any classical algorithm, as that would refute the strong exponential time hypothesis.

assertions.value: The authors state that both algorithms require a quantum random access memory, of which experimental implementations do not yet exist.
quotes: Both algorithms require a quantum random access memory (QRAM)
of which experimental implementations do not yet exist.

papers.title_in_file: Recent Developments and Perspectives in Variational Quantum Eigensolvers for Molecular Electronic Structure: Methods, Tradeoffs, and Benchmarking
papers.what_it_is: Survey of VQE methods for molecular electronic structure with small illustrative benchmarks.

assertions.value: The authors state that their illustrative benchmarks show savings in parameter count do not automatically imply savings in total computational cost, and that threshold-based conclusions are strongly basis set dependent.
quotes: Our illustrative benchmarks reinforce this broader point: savings in parameter count do not automatically imply savings in total computational cost, and threshold-based conclusions are strongly basis set dependent.

assertions.value: The authors state that no single ansatz or workflow is uniformly best across the methods reviewed.
quotes: Across the methods reviewed here, a clear theme is that no single ansatz or workflow is uniformly best.

assertions.value: The authors state that measurement overhead remains a central bottleneck and that compactness gains of adaptive ansatzes can be offset by repeated gradient evaluation.
quotes: Measurement overhead remains a central bottleneck, and the compactness gains of adaptive ansatzes can be offset by repeated gradient evaluation.

assertions.value: The authors state their view that the strongest case for chemically useful VQE does not lie in equilibrium single-reference molecules.
quotes: In our view, the strongest case for chemically useful VQE does not lie in equilibrium single-reference molecules,

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning in Multi-Qubit Phase-Space Part I: Foundations
papers.what_it_is: Theory paper building a phase-space formalism for many-qubit systems aimed at QML.

assertions.value: The authors state they prove that for qubits Stinespring's theorem can be realised in phase-space via an extended kernel.
quotes: proving that for qubits the Stinespring's theorem can be realised in phase-space via an extended kernel.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 6 summary of derivations; proof not checked by the reader

assertions.value: The authors state that Hilbert-space and phase-space representations encode the same exponential number of degrees of freedom, so the formalism does not eliminate the exponential overhead.
quotes: Hilbert-space and phase-space representations ultimately encode the same exponential number of degrees of freedom.
While this does not eliminate the exponential overhead, it recasts it as bandwidth rather than coordinate dimension.

assertions.value: The authors state that a many-qubit phase space could be a promising avenue for neural-network-based inference and control, as the first in a series with practical modelling left to future work.
quotes: A many-qubit phase space could be a promising avenue for neural-network-based inference and control because its structure is more amenable to neural network approximation.
As the first in a series of papers, this work develops a phase-space formalism for many-qubit quantum machine learning.
assertions.certainty_reason: Prospect stated without a QML experiment

papers.title_in_file: From Classical Data to Quantum Advantage - Quantum Policy Evaluation on Quantum Hardware
papers.what_it_is: Learns a quantum bandit environment from classical data and runs quantum policy evaluation on IonQ hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the two-armed bandit benchmark it is possible to learn circuit parameters that result in satisfactory model performance on real quantum hardware.
quotes: Our experiments indicate that, for the two-armed bandit benchmark, it is possible to learn circuit parameters that result in satisfactory model performance on real quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that only the most basic circuit configuration in QPE produced the expected outcomes on hardware, and that the effect of noise becomes more severe as n grows.
quotes: However, only the most basic circuit configuration in QPE produced the expected outcomes.
As expected, the effect becomes more severe as n grows.

assertions.value: The authors state they tried n = 3 and n = 4 on IonQ forte-1 and ran each circuit 300 times.
quotes: we tried n = 3 and n = 4, which resulted in QPE circuits with 5 and 6 qubits consisting of 412 and 883 one- and two-qubit gates, respectively.
We ran each circuit for 300 times to produce an empirical estimate of the measurement distribution.

assertions.value: The paper states that quantum policy evaluation is quadratically more efficient than an analogous classical Monte Carlo estimation, a result it attributes to earlier work.
quotes: Quantum policy evaluation (QPE) is a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm which is quadratically more efficient than an analogous classical Monte Carlo estimation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to earlier work in the introduction
